title: Durablity
i was burning a ton of tokens on silly stuff
partialText:
<p>has anyone else noticed they're chewing through claude tokens way faster than they should be? anthropic just announced they're <a href="https://x.com/trq212/status/2037254607001559305" rel="noopener noreferrer">tightening the 5-hour session limits during peak hours</a> and it made me actually look at where my tokens were going.</p>

<p>turns out most of it was waste. claude was reading files it had no reason to read like lock files, build artifacts, node_modules, coverage reports, media files. every time it explored the codebase it was burning tokens on stuff that would never help it write better code.</p>

<p>i added a <code>.claudeignore</code> file:<br>
</p>

<div class="highlight js-code-highlight">
<pre class="highlight plaintext"><code># Dependencies
node_modules/
.pnp.*

# Build artifacts
.next/
out/
build/
dist/

# Lock files (huge, no value to read)
package-lock.json
pnpm-lock.yaml
yarn.lock

# Minified bundles
*.min.js
*.min.css

# Generated code
next-env.d.ts
*.tsbuildinfo

# Caches
.cache/
__pycache__/
coverage/

# Environment / secrets
.env*
.vercel/

# Large non-code files
*.gif
*.mov
*.mp4
*.png
*.jpg
</code></pre>

</div>



<p>it works like <code>.gitignore</code> but for claude's file exploration. claude won't read or search anything that matches.</p>

<p>the other thing that helps is keeping <code>CLAUDE.md</code> lean. mine is about 145 lines with architecture essentials, key conventions, common gotchas. not a novel. every line of CLAUDE.md gets loaded into context at the start of every conversation, so bloat there costs you tokens on every single interaction.</p>

<p>i'm still seeing how much this helps. they're obviously just clamping down.</p>

<p>if you're on the Max plan and it still feels like you're burning through it, check what claude is actually reading. you might be feeding it your pnpm-lock.yaml on every exploration.</p>

<p>markdown edited in <a href="//ginsberg.ai">ginsberg.ai</a></p>
